question.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the typical 'factors' used in smart-beta factor investing?

explanation.text: The Logic: Discretion is the hallmark of discretionary active management — smart beta is rule-based and systematic. Value, Quality, Momentum, Size, Volatility are the canonical factors. The Trap: The line between 'rule design' (allowed in smart beta) and 'discretion' (disqualifies smart beta) is subtle — but ongoing discretion isn't smart-beta. Manager's Pro-Tip: If a product's factor weights change quarterly based on manager view, it's active quant — not smart beta — even if it markets itself as smart beta.
